- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.5) — add 3–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment shifts — adjust 3–5 days ahead by subtracting 2–3% if sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– > 0.3), reduce forecast variance by 10–15% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
- If forecast exceeds true outcome by > 10% in 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — use sentiment-weighted moving average (last 7 days) for smoothing.
